Bulgarian

[edit]
Bulgarian Wikipedia has an article on:
балет
Wikipedia bg

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Italian balletto (“small dance”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [bɐˈlɛt]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɛt

Noun

[edit]

бале́т • (balét) m

  1. ballet

Declension

[edit]
Declension of бале́т
singular plural
indefinite бале́т
balét 		бале́ти
baléti
definite
(subject form) 		бале́тът
balétǎt 		бале́тите
balétite
definite
(object form) 		бале́та
baléta
count form — бале́та
baléta

Related terms

[edit]
  • балери́на (balerína, “ballet-dancer”)

References

[edit]
  • “балет”, in Речник на българския език [Dictionary of the Bulgarian Language] (in Bulgarian), Sofia: Bulgarian Academy of Sciences, 2014
  • “балет”, in Речник на българския език [Dictionary of the Bulgarian Language] (in Bulgarian), Chitanka, 2010

  1. ballet

Russian

[edit]
Russian Wikipedia has an article on:
балет
Wikipedia ru

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French ballet. Further from Italian balletto, from Latin ballō + -ittus (whence Italian -etto, French -et).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [bɐˈlʲet]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Saint Petersburg):(file)
  • Rhymes: -et

Noun

[edit]

бале́т • (balét) m inan (genitive бале́та, nominative plural бале́ты, genitive plural бале́тов, relational adjective бале́тный)

  1. ballet

Declension

[edit]
Declension of бале́т (inan masc-form hard-stem accent-a) 
singular plural
nominative бале́т
balét 		бале́ты
baléty
genitive бале́та
baléta 		бале́тов

balétami
prepositional бале́те
baléte 		бале́тах
balétax

Related terms

[edit]
  • балери́на f anim (balerína)
  • балетме́йстер m anim (baletméjster)
  • кордебале́т m (kordebalét)

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Eastern Mari: балет (baĺet)
  • → Georgian: ბალეტი (baleṭi)
  • → Kazakh: балет (balet)
  • → Mongolian: балет (balet)

[edit]

Further reading

[edit]
